'''''Lysimachia ephemerum''''', the '''willow-leaved loosestrife''' or '''milky loosestrife''',<ref name = EOL>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/25466/Lysimachia-ephemerum/Details | title = Milky loosestrife | website = EOL.org | publisher = Encyclopedia of Life | access-date = 21 March 2021}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the primrose [[family (botany)|family]] Primulaceae, [[native species|native]] to France, Spain, Portugal and Morocco.<ref name = POWO>{{cite web | url = https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:701110-1
| title = ''Lysimachia ephemerum'' L. | publisher = Plants of the World Online | access-date = 21 March 2021}}</ref> Against grey-green foliage this [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] bears erect racemes of delicate white flowers with purple stamens on {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on}} stems in early summer. It is cultivated as an ornamental plant, and holds the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/25466/Lysimachia-ephemerum/Details | title = ''Lysimachia ephemerum'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> It requires a position in full sun, and reliably moist soil.
